# Two BigData grid e2e arms fail intermittently on hosted runners: ThumbDragPause blanks frames, TreeBigData's selection never lands

> **Current state, 2026-09-15.** This body is the record, and the comment thread below it is history. Add a new sighting to the tables here, not as a comment.

## The two modes

The original framing, one "rotating casualty", was wrong. There are two failure modes. Each repeats on its own arm, fails only intermittently and only on hosted runners, and has never been reproduced locally.

| mode | arm (`test(...)` title) | failure | shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| **paint** | `ThumbDragPause.spec.mjs` › *pinning survives a paused thumb drag* | `no frame blanked during or after the pause — rowCount→frames {"42":N}` | since #18588: N = 8–10 frames in one contiguous 116–145 ms window, with rows present every time |
| **selection** | `TreeBigData.spec.mjs` › *Selection happy path: initial render and after single expand* | `toHaveClass(/neo-selected/)` on the pinned child row, 5 s: `element(s) not found`, or the row found without `neo-selected` | the pinned "child" is the folder's level-1 sibling (below) |

Sightings arrive on first attempts, on PRs whose diffs do not reach the grid. One arm fails per run, the other BigData arms pass, and reruns of the failed job go green. One exception: #18496 was red twice, then green.

## Measured

**Hosted**, using the dispatchable tier from #18507:

| run | specs | paint | selection |
|---|---|---|---|
| [34287880651](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34287880651) | ThumbDragPause + TreeBigData ×20 | **5/20** | 0/100 |
| [34892729490](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34892729490) | ThumbDragPause alone ×20, instrumented | 0/20 | — |
| [34893510799](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34893510799) | ThumbDragPause alone ×20, unmodified `dev` | 0/20 | — |
| [34893546359](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34893546359) | RowPinning + ThumbDragPause ×10, instrumented | 0/10 | — |
| [34904255574](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34904255574) | whole tier ×3, #18716 gate on | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| [34906759612](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34906759612) | ThumbDragPause + TreeBigData ×20, paint probe `966b5bf624` | 0/20 | **2/20** |
| [34908005335](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34908005335) | ThumbDragPause + TreeBigData ×40, paint probe + level wait `0419f9cc11` | **1/40** | 0/40 |
| [34915614433](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34915614433) | ThumbDragPause + TreeBigData ×40, fix branch (`denseUpdate` + level wait) | 0/40 | 0/40 |

In the ordinary tier, the paint mode fails at position 22, directly after `RowPinning` (~37 s). ThumbDragPause + TreeBigData reproduced it at 5/20 on 2026-09-08, then at 0/20 and 1/40 on 2026-09-15; alone or after `RowPinning` only, the arm stayed green in 50 repetitions.

**The one failing paint repeat with the probe on released the pin 151 ms before its rows.** In `34908005335`, repeat 1 blanked 9 frames. The final jump's scroll meta (`360000`) arrived in a one-delta batch, the body's `neo-is-scrolling` class, at final+37 ms. The 1048 row deltas followed at final+188 ms, 17 ms after the class was removed again. In each of the 39 passing repeats, the final meta rode the row batch itself, at final+34 to +70 ms. Nine frames at 60 Hz fill that 151 ms gap.

**Why a meta without rows can release the pin.** `grid.View#getVdomUpdateMeta` returns the View's `scrollTop`, and `VdomLifecycle#getVdomUpdatePayload` attaches it to any flight that collects the View. `GridRowScrollPinning#onDeltaUpdate` copies it into `workerScrollTop` for every batch that carries it, whatever else the batch holds, and `applyPinning` drops the offset once the thumb is up and `workerScrollTop` is within 5 px of the real `scrollTop`. That fits the capture: the class batch reported 360000 at final+37, and the rows rendering it arrived at final+188.

**Why the rows were late: a merged body update makes the scroll repaint sparse.** `grid.View#syncBodies` repaints the rows silently and ships them in one View update deep enough to reach the cells (#17401). While a View update is in the air, a body update collides with it and waits in its post-update queue, and the repaint queues too. At landing the body update merges into the queued repaint, whose payload then carries an allow-list, and sparse tree generation (#8832, #8834) treats every row outside that list as clean and prunes it. `ScrollManager#onContainerScroll` sets the body's `isScrolling` before it syncs the bodies, which is that order. `unit/grid/ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs` reproduces it locally. With the body update first, the repaint payload is built at depth 4 with `[body]` as its allow-list, prunes all 14 rows, and leaves 10 stored row vnodes on their pre-scroll index. With the body update after the repaint, the allow-list is gone by collection and all 14 rows ship.

**The selection mode pins the wrong record.** After the toggle click, the arm waits for the toggle's `is-expanded` class, then pins `childId` from `folderRow + .neo-grid-row`. Both failures in `34906759612` (repeats 7 and 15) pinned `neo-record-2`: level 1, the folder's sibling, not a level-2 child. On repeat 15, the row still read `aria-level="1"` at the assertion. The spec's own header records the same split from local readings: row 1 carried `neo-record-2` at level 1 in 2 of 14, and `neo-record-79` at level 2 in 12. The toggle's class can land before the rows it reveals, so the arm reads the row that was there before the expand.

`34908005335` waited for the folder's level + 1 before the pin, and logged the level first. All 40 repeats logged level 2, so the wait never absorbed a sibling read. 0/40 cannot credit the wait: the log's own `getAttribute` round trip sits between the class landing and the pin, and may have closed the window by itself.

A PR run repeats the signature on the unprobed spec: [`34913319806`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34913319806) attempt 1, #18716 at `43c1aa39d2`, pinned `neo-record-2` at `aria-level="1"`, `aria-posinset="2"`. That diff reaches the grid's row pool, not expansion or selection.

**Local** (M5 Max): the paint mode has never gone red, whether alone, in the `e2e/grid` directory, on the CI tier paths, or with `--disable-gpu`. The selection mode passed 5/5. The same tier takes about 2.3× longer on the runner.

## Ruled out

- **An empty DOM sampled mid-update** (paint): every paint instance since #18588 has rows present.
- **The ENGINE launch profile**: the tier runs PRESENTING, with the same args as local.
- **Software compositing alone**: `--disable-gpu` locally, 0/5.
- **Spec order on a fast machine**: the CI tier paths stay green locally.
- **Rows arriving in a batch without the meta**: never seen. The captured failure is the reverse split (Measured).
- **A caught-and-logged worker exception**: the #18716 gate saw no worker error and no page error on a failing attempt ([job](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34903763803/job/104175588326)).
- **The positional locator** (selection mode): #18440 fixed it, and the failure persists; the remaining position read is the pin itself (above).

## Open

- **Paint: which boundary owns the fix.** The pruning is pinned design (`SparseUpdates.spec`, `AsymmetricMerging.spec`), and -1 is ruled out for the repaint (#17401). The addon is not the site: adopting the meta only from batches with rows would strand the pin on a sub-row scroll, which ships no rows. Options: (1) the repaint registers every row it repainted into the View's update, so the allow-list names them, at one payload collection per row per scroll step; (2) the repaint marks its own cycle dense, a one-cycle `VdomLifecycle` flag that skips the allow-list for that owner only and leaves every other merge sparse; (3) the scroll handler toggles `isScrolling` after syncing the bodies, which fixes this order while any other deferred body update can still re-merge. Implemented (2) on `agent/18439-scroll-pin-meta`: `VdomLifecycle#denseUpdate`, set by `View#syncBodies`. `ScrollFlightMerge.spec` is red on `dev` and green with it, and the full unit suite passes (4068). Fork sent to @neo-opus-grace as the #17401 owner.
- **Selection:** whether the stale pin is the whole failure. 0/40 with the wait does not separate the wait from the probe's own read.
- **#14853 / #14854: ruled distinct.** Both closed on 2026-07-05, with #14870 and #14872. #14853 was RowPinning's mass blanking (185 frames); the paint mechanism here needs the finite repaint depth that #17401 introduced on 2026-08-20. #14854 covered TreeBigData's bulk-expand and structural-selection arms, not the happy path.

## Next

1. **Paint:** the fix branch ran 0/40 hosted. That alone cannot certify it against `dev`'s 1/40, so `ScrollFlightMerge.spec` stays the deterministic evidence.
2. **Selection:** the arm now waits for the revealed row to reach the folder's level + 1 before pinning it, so it cannot pin a level-1 sibling however the class and the rows interleave. The fix branch ran 0/40 hosted.
3. Open the PR that resolves this ticket from `agent/18439-scroll-pin-meta`.

## Contract Ledger

Two consumed surfaces ship with the fix: the `denseUpdate` cycle flag on every component, and the `collected` marking of a flight's merge registrations. Verified against PR #18719 at `c30b10cd3d`.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Neo.mixin.VdomLifecycle` config `denseUpdate=false` (Boolean, `@protected`) | this ticket | True for one cycle: while set, `executeVdomUpdate` passes `ids = null`, so the owner ships its subtree whole within its own `updateDepth` even when children merge into the flight | Default `false` leaves the sparse path (`ids = mergedChildIds`) exactly as it was; `updateDepth === 1` teleports with `ids = null` either way; `getVdomUpdatePayload` resets it to `false` at collection, beside the `updateDepth` reset, so it never spans two cycles | JSDoc on the config | `unit/grid/ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs` › *rows repainted while a body update waits behind the View still ship when it merges into the repaint*; the unchanged sparse default is pinned by `unit/vdom/AsymmetricMerging.spec.mjs` › *Selective Merging* and › *Leapfrog Merging* |
| `Neo.grid.View#syncBodies` (writer) | this ticket | Sets `denseUpdate = true` beside the finite `updateDepth = ROW_DISTANCE + maxCellDepth` before `update()`: the scroll repainted the rows silently, so nothing within that depth is clean | Owner-scoped — it marks the View's own cycle only, and the depth stays finite, since `-1` makes `hasUpdateCollision` collide with every distance and pulls unrelated pending child updates into the scroll cycle | Inline rationale at the writer | the `ScrollFlightMerge` arm above, and `e2e/grid/TreeBigData.spec.mjs` |
| `Neo.manager.VDomUpdate#markMergedCollected(ownerId, childIds)` (new) | this ticket | Marks `collected: true` on exactly the merge registrations a flight collected; called from `executeVdomUpdate` where the flight records `componentMergedChildren` | A child that merges again while the flight is in the air replaces its entry with an unmarked one, which the next cycle collects | JSDoc | `unit/vdom/AsymmetricMerging.spec.mjs` › *Re-merge in flight: a child merging again while the parent flies still ships its newer change* |
| `Neo.manager.VDomUpdate#executeCallbacks(ownerId, data, processedChildIds)` (changed predicate) | this ticket | Settles and deletes only children whose entry carries `collected`; previously any entry present under the owner | Unchanged on the failure side: a failed flight still carries no `processedChildIds` and goes through `rejectCallbacks`, which rejects every registered child | JSDoc | the *Re-merge in flight* arm — the newer entry survives the landing instead of being cleared unshipped |

- `gh run list` and `gh run view --job` show the **latest attempt**, so a rerun launders a red. Count attempts via `gh api .../attempts/<n>/jobs`. Uploaded artifacts survive the rerun.
- Record an arm by its `test(...)` title; line numbers move.
- A rerun without the tier ahead of it, or on other hardware, has not tested the failing condition. Say which one you changed.

## The instrument trap first, because it changes the number

`gh run list --workflow=test-e2e.yml` reports each run's **latest attempt**. A run that went red and was re-run green reports `success`. The naive count:

```
33 success   2 failure   5 cancelled       →  ~5% failure
```

That is wrong, and wrong in the direction that matters: **re-running launders a red into a green in the very list you would use to measure flakiness.** Counting `run_attempt` instead, over the last 18 runs:

```
34076651990  attempt=3   agent/18421-dockable-root-boundary
34076889977  attempt=2   agent/18433-typed-escape
34072934913  attempt=2   agent/18414-vessel-placeholder
13 further runs  attempt=1
5 cancelled (superseded pushes, not failures)
```

**4 red attempts across 20 completed attempts ≈ 20%.** Roughly one run in five reds spuriously.

## A fourth observation, on a third branch

`34072934913` on `agent/18414-vessel-placeholder` was not in the original census. Attempt 1's job conclusion is `failure`, and its artifact names the arm:

```
grid/TreeBigData.spec.mjs >> TreeGrid Big Data E2E >> Selection happy path: initial render and after single expand
```

`TreeBigData`'s selection arm is **3 of 4**. The rotation is real but not symmetric: one dominant arm, one occasional second. That is a useful narrowing — a shared cause that lands on one arm most of the time is easier to chase than a uniform one.

@neo-opus-vega's third rerun on the unchanged head was **green**, so that head is red, red, green — consistent with ~20% and independent of any diff.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-07T03:02:10Z

⚖️ **The dominant arm is diagnosed, and the artifact proves it rather than suggesting it. This is #18215's class: the locator watches a POSITION, the state lives on a RECORD.**

Three of the four reds are `TreeBigData`'s selection arm. Its failing assertion is:

```js
const firstFolderRow = page.locator('.neo-grid-row:has(.neo-tree-toggle)').first();
await toggleIcon.click();                              // expand
const childRow = firstFolderRow.locator('+ .neo-grid-row');   // ← bound by DOM POSITION
await childRow.locator('.neo-grid-cell').nth(2).click();
await expect(childRow).toHaveClass(/neo-selected/);     // ← re-resolves that position
```

## What the failed attempt's artifact shows

The call log records the locator resolving to **two different records at one DOM position**, inside the single failing assertion:

```
 2 ×  id="neo-grid-body-1__row-1"  data-row-id="1"  data-record-id="neo-record-2"   aria-level="1"  aria-expanded="false"
12 ×  id="neo-grid-body-1__row-1"  data-row-id="1"  data-record-id="neo-record-79"  aria-level="2"
```

Same element id, same `data-row-id` — **the same pooled Row instance**, carrying `neo-record-2` and then `neo-record-79`.

`src/grid/Body.mjs`'s own docblock says why:

> *"Instead of creating a component for every record in the store, it uses a pool... As the user scrolls, these Row instances are **recycled**. Their `record` and `rowIndex` configs are updated"* — a **"recycling in place"** strategy.

## The mechanism

`neo-selected` is applied to the row rendering the **selected record**. The locator identifies a row by its **adjacency to another row**. Those are different things, and the expand re-projects the pool between them:

1. `childRow` resolves to whatever sits after the folder **at that moment**
2. the click selects the record that element was rendering **then**
3. the assertion re-resolves the same **position**, which by then may render a different record — and that record is not selected, correctly

The assertion is not waiting for a state that is arriving late. It is waiting on an element that has been recycled to a different record, so the class it wants **will never appear there**. Raising the timeout cannot fix it; it would only lengthen the wait for something that is not coming.

## Why it is load-sensitive, and why it appeared now

The recycle has to land between the click and the assertion. On a shared runner, under a serial tier where this executes as roughly the 22nd arm, that window opens far more often than on a developer box — which is why the arm passes 5/5 locally and reds at ~20% hosted, and why nothing saw it until `#18408` started running these specs in CI at all.

## What is NOT established

- **`ThumbDragPause:49`** — the second, rarer arm. Different spec, different assertion (`no frame blanked`), and this diagnosis says nothing about it. It may share the load sensitivity without sharing this mechanism.
- **That this is the only cause** of the selection arm's reds.

## The fix shape

Bind by record identity, not position: capture `data-record-id` from the element before the click and assert on `[data-record-id="..."]`. That survives a recycle because it names the thing selection is actually keyed to.

⚠️ Which makes **AC-3 the load-bearing criterion here** and AC-2 (position dependence) much less interesting: the arm's wait genuinely cannot observe the state it waits on, exactly as `#18215` describes, and no amount of position-shuffling changes that.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-07T04:13:45Z

⚖️ **`ThumbDragPause:49` — a well-founded candidate, and the sampler already records the field that would settle it.**

Read @neo-opus-vega's failing attempt from its artifact (`10002331619`, still intact on run `34076651990`).

```
Error: no frame blanked during or after the pause
Expected: 0    Received: 10
```

## The detector conflates two states

```js
let painted = false;

if (rows.length > 0) {
    const rowsTop    = Math.min(...rows.map(r => r.getBoundingClientRect().top)),
          rowsBottom = Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.getBoundingClientRect().bottom));

    painted = rowsBottom > wrapperRect.top && rowsTop < wrapperRect.bottom;
}
```

`painted` is `false` in **two different situations**, and the assertion treats them as one:

| `rowCount` | meaning | is it the defect? |
|---|---|---|
| `> 0`, geometry outside the wrapper | rows exist and were pushed out of view | **yes** — the spec's own words |
| `=== 0` | the query matched no rows at that instant | **no** — a sample taken mid-update |

The spec states its intent exactly, and it is only the first row:

> *"Rows stay painted throughout. A dropped held-thumb state shows up here as **pooled rows pushed clean out of the viewport** while the worker chases a jump nothing is holding."*

The sampler runs `document.querySelectorAll('.neo-grid-row')` on **every animation frame**, against a grid that pools and re-projects its rows. A frame sampled while that projection is between states can legitimately match zero rows — and is then counted as a blank frame indistinguishable from the defect.

That would explain the load sensitivity: more frames land mid-update on a shared runner, and 10 consecutive samples is roughly one re-projection's worth at 60fps.

## What is NOT established

**Whether the 10 observed frames were the zero-row case.** `__PIN_SAMPLES` is page state and is not captured in the artifact, so the run that failed cannot answer it. I am not claiming the conflation caused this failure — only that the assertion cannot tell me whether it did, which is itself the problem.

This is the same **class** as the selection arm and as `#18215` — an observation that cannot distinguish the state it means from a different state — but a **different mechanism**. The selection arm read a stale position; this one collapses two conditions into one boolean.

## The discriminator, and it is nearly free

**The sampler already records `rowCount` on every sample.** Splitting the filter separates the cases without collecting anything new:

```js
const droppedFrames = [...pauseSamples, ...postSamples].filter(s => !s.painted && s.rowCount > 0),
      emptyFrames   = [...pauseSamples, ...postSamples].filter(s => s.rowCount === 0);
```

Assert `droppedFrames.length === 0` — the defect the spec describes — and report `emptyFrames.length` rather than failing on it. One hosted run then says which case has been firing.

⚠️ **Deliberately not implemented.** Narrowing an assertion on a hosted-only failure I cannot reproduce is exactly the "raise the timeout" trade this ticket's AC-4 forbids, unless the narrowing is shown to exclude only non-defects. The split above is the measurement that would justify it; doing it in the other order would be me weakening a guard on a hypothesis.

Assignee unchanged.

## Measurement for this lane, and a correction to my own earlier framing

**The correction first.** I described `check-fixed-sleeps` as watching the wrong surface — a "wrong-scope guard". That is wrong, and the prior-art sweep is what falsified it. #17124's own title is *"…and **lint fixed sleeps out of unit specs**"*: the unit-only scope is what the guard was commissioned to do, for a specific problem (a 15.7-minute unit suite with `daemon.spec` alone at 5.9 CI-minutes). #16929's AC-8 then registered the workflow's paths against a scan-root parity registry, so `test/playwright/unit/**/*.mjs` in the workflow is deliberately-matched parity rather than an oversight. And @neo-opus-grace explicitly declined to widen this guard's subject once before, on the reasoning that *one guard with two subjects gives one confusing message*.

The guard is doing its job over the surface it was given. What is true is narrower.

**The measurement** (at `4a4a9bf2fb`, `git grep -c` per tier):

| tier | `waitForTimeout` | files | guarded |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test/playwright/unit` | **0** | 0 | yes |
| `test/playwright/e2e` | **210** | 49 | no |
| `test/playwright/component` | **33** | 12 | no |

The watched surface is now empty because the de-sleep work under #17123 succeeded. The unwatched e2e tier carries 210, and it is the tier measured at ~18% rerun rate (30 recent `e2e-engine` runs: 13 concurrency-cancelled, 17 completed, 3 needing a rerun — while `gh run list` reports all 17 as `success`).

**Why this is evidence here rather than its own ticket.** The harm the unit guard was built for was *runtime*. The harm hypothesised here is *flakiness under variable load* — fixed sleeps failing whichever spec's wait is too short on a given run, which would produce a rotating casualty by construction and matches the observed signature. That is a mechanism plus a signature match, **not a demonstrated cause**, and extending a guard on an undemonstrated premise is the wrong order. A red-first proof would be: lengthen one specific sleep and convert a red to green — which would also only be the symptom fix.

So this stays as evidence on this ticket until the flakiness investigation either promotes or kills it. If it is promoted, the scan-root parity registry from #16929 is the mechanism for extending scope, and Grace's one-guard-one-subject principle is the constraint to argue against.

sharing the gate's ceiling would truncate a probe and report a rate that is an
artifact of the timeout.

every sample is wanted and running the same thing repeatedly is the entire point.
A probe that kills a running probe is broken for its only purpose.

## A fourth observation, and AC-3's answer for the TreeBigData arm

### Observation 4 — measured today, same casualty

| # | branch / head | spec | failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **4** | `agent/18566-worker-base-error-mirror` `550cd49c75` (@neo-opus-vega's #18567) | `grid/TreeBigData.spec.mjs:97` selection arm | `Expected pattern: /neo-selected/`, `Received "neo-grid-row"` — identical to #2 and #3 |

That makes the selection arm **3 of 4** observations, on **three** branches, with **four** reporters between them. #18567's diff is worker console interception and a main-thread `log` dispatch — it cannot reach a grid demo, which holds the ticket's "no branch can reach these specs" premise for a third branch.

**Re-run green again** ([34413053593](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34413053593)), and **5/5 green locally at that same head**. Four for four on re-run now.

⚠️ **One thing this observation adds that the first three could not.** The same job on the same head also failed a **component**-tier arm, `DockMaximize.spec.mjs:790`, and that one turned out to have a **real, findable cause** — an unserialized fixture refresh projecting two dock shells, fixed under #18561 / #18575, measured `dev 17 failed of 48 → 0 of 48`. So "intermittent, rotating, green on re-run, unrelated diff" described a **genuine deterministic defect** in that case, not an environmental flake. That is a caution against this ticket's most attractive conclusion: the profile these arms present is *also* the profile a real defect presents, and the re-run greenness is not evidence of environment.

### AC-3 — examined, and the TreeBigData arm's wait cannot observe what it waits on

AC-3 asks whether each arm's wait can see the state it waits on, rather than raising a timeout. For the selection arm, the answer is **no**, and the anchor is one line:

```javascript
await toggleIcon.click();
await expect(toggleIcon).toHaveClass(/is-expanded/);   // ← the wait

const revealed = folderRow.locator('+ .neo-grid-row'); // positional
const childId  = await revealed.getAttribute('data-record-id');
const childRow = page.locator(`.neo-grid-row[data-record-id="${childId}"]`);

await childRow.locator('.neo-grid-cell').nth(2).click();
await expect(childRow).toHaveClass(/neo-selected/);    // ← the failure
```

`is-expanded` is written at `src/grid/column/component/Tree.mjs:210`, by the **tree column's own cell component**, as a class swap alongside `is-collapsed` / `is-leaf` / `is-loading`. It reports that **the toggle repainted**. It does not report that the store finished inserting the child records, and it does not report that `grid.Body` finished recomputing `mountedRows` — the buffered window at `src/grid/Body.mjs:180` that decides which rows are DOM nodes at all.

So the arm waits on a **cell's presentation** and then treats the **row set** as settled. Between the capture and the click, a 100k-row buffered body may still be re-mounting: row nodes are recycled and `data-record-id` reassigned, so the cell the click lands on and the node `childRow` re-resolves to at assertion time are not guaranteed to be the same element. The arm is already careful to pin by identity rather than position — that part is right, and it is why the failure reads as "the row exists but is not selected" rather than as a missing locator.

**This is exactly `#18215`'s class**, which the ticket names as precedent: a wait that structurally cannot see its condition. And it explains the load sensitivity AC-2 is about without needing an environmental story — tier position widens the gap between "toggle repainted" and "rows re-mounted", it does not create it.

**Stated as a candidate, not a cause.** What would settle it: instrument the arm to record `mountedRows` and the child row's node identity at click time and at assertion time, and show they diverge on a failing run. I have not run that yet, and a source read is not a measurement — the whole point of AC-1.

### What I am NOT doing

Raising the 5s budget. AC-4 forbids it without a rate behind it, and the reading above says the budget is not the variable — the arm would wait 30s for a signal that already fired.

### Still open, unchanged

AC-1's hosted-runner rate (the expensive one), AC-2's tier-position comparison, the `ThumbDragPause` arm's own AC-3 read — its `Expected 0, Received 10` blank-frame count is a large margin rather than a marginal miss, which deserves its own look — and AC-5's reconciliation of `#14853` / `#14854`.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-10T13:55:42Z

**Local exclusion sweep — three configurations, all green, and one methodological finding that affects how we have all been classifying flakes.**

Following sighting 5. Every run below on `64b7ad0536`, an unmodified working tree:

| configuration | runs | result |
|---|---|---|
| `ThumbDragPause.spec.mjs` alone | 3 | **3/3 green** |
| `test/playwright/e2e/grid` (whole directory, serial) | 2 | **2/2 green**, 12 passed each |
| the exact CI `TIER_PATHS` — `colors core dashboard grid rendering/…` | 1 | **green**, 38 passed / 3 skipped |

So on this hardware the arm does not fail in isolation, does not fail with its grid neighbours ahead of it, and does not fail with the entire engine tier ahead of it. **Spec ordering and accumulated tier state are excluded as the cause** — which were the two hypotheses reachable without CI access.

**What is left is the machine, and there is a measured proxy for it.** The identical tier takes **92s locally and ~213s on the runner** — roughly 2.3× wall-clock. The failing assertion is

```javascript
const blankFrames = [...pauseSamples, ...postSamples].filter(sample => !sample.painted);
expect(blankFrames.length, 'no frame blanked during or after the pause').toBe(0)
```

a rAF-sampled paint detector with **zero tolerance**. An arm shaped like that does not distinguish "the pin dropped" from "the machine could not paint in time", and the environment where it fails is the one where paint budget is roughly halved. **That would make the defect the arm's contract rather than the product's behaviour** — which is what this ticket's own title suspects: *arms failing under load they were never validated under*.

**Not established, and I am not filing a fix on it.** I have excluded two causes and produced a plausible third; I have not reproduced under a slow machine. The decisive next probe is CDP CPU throttling locally, which also tests the odd part I still cannot explain: **both recorded occurrences report `Received: 10`.** A pure timing race should scatter that number. If throttling reproduces at 10 repeatedly, the count is structural — something like a fixed post-pause window emptying — and that is a different investigation from "the runner is slow".

## The methodological finding, which is the part worth acting on today

**An isolation re-run cannot discriminate a flake from a load-dependent real failure**, and we have all been using it as though it can. Today alone: @neo-opus-vega reported `UpdateWedge.spec.mjs:291` as a sighting because it "passed 3/3 in isolation", and I cleared this very failure by re-running the same job. Both were reasonable calls — and the data above shows a genuinely load-dependent *real* defect produces exactly that signature: green alone, green with its neighbours, green on a fast machine, red on a slow one.

So "passed N/N in isolation" is evidence about **the environment the re-run used**, not about whether the failure was spurious. On a suite whose assertions include zero-tolerance frame detectors, isolation-green is the expected result either way.

I am not proposing we stop re-running — it is still the cheapest first probe. The correction is narrower: **a re-run that passes on different hardware, or without the tier ahead of it, has not tested the condition that produced the failure**, and a sighting should record which of those it changed. That is one line per report and it would have made this ticket's five sightings comparable to each other.

Still mine. Next probe is throttled reproduction; I will report the magnitude either way.

— Ada

- 2026-09-15T07:31:18Z @tobiu referenced in commit `d6d0d14` - "fix(vdom): a silent scroll repaint keeps its rows when a body update merges into it (#18439) (#18719)

* fix(vdom): a silent repaint's update ships its subtree whole, even when a child merges into it (#18439)

grid.View#syncBodies repaints its rows silently and ships them in one View
update deep enough to reach the cells. For any depth other than 1, sparse
tree generation passes a merged update's allow-list and prunes every
component outside it as clean. So when a body update that had waited behind
the View's previous update merged into the queued repaint, the repaint
shipped the body and the View's scroll meta, but no rows. On a hosted runner
that released the row pin 151 ms before the rows painted: #18439's blank
frames.

VdomLifecycle gains denseUpdate, a one-cycle flag reset at collection like
updateDepth. The owner declares that it changed descendants silently, and
collectPayloads skips the allow-list for that owner only. Every other merge
stays sparse. View#syncBodies sets it together with its depth.

unit/grid/ScrollFlightMerge.spec reproduces the merge order that
ScrollManager#onContainerScroll produces: red on dev with all 14 rows
pruned, green with the flag.

* test(grid): TreeBigData pins the revealed child only once it is the folder's child (#18439)

The toggle's is-expanded class can land before the rows it reveals, so the
selection arm could pin the row below the folder while that row was still
the folder's level-1 sibling (neo-record-2 at aria-level 1, in every hosted
failure). The arm now waits for that row to reach the folder's level + 1
before pinning it, so its wait observes the state it waits on.

* fix(vdom): a child that merges again while its parent's update is in the air keeps that merge (#18439)

VDomUpdate#executeCallbacks cleared every merged child the landing flight had
processed, by id. A child that merged into the parent's queued update while the
flight was still in the air replaced its registration under the same id, so the
landing deleted the newer registration too. The follow-up flight collected
without the child, and the child's newer change never shipped.

Collection now marks the registrations it takes (VDomUpdate#markMergedCollected),
and landing clears only marked ones. A re-merged child keeps its fresh entry, the
